messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm going to run a blackbox rate-limit validation in staging this afternoon. Goal: validate per-org and per-key token-bucket behavior under synthetic traffic and make sure our fallback routing doesn't saturate Dedicated. Starting at ~18:00 UTC. Will post plan and hooks.

sam: Nice. What's the traffic pattern? short spikes, long tail, or steady high qps?

alex: Plan in brief: three phases — 1) short sharp spikes (~500 RPS for 30s) to exercise burst allowance, 2) sustained medium load (~120 RPS for 20m) to exercise refill logic and backbone, 3) multi-key churn (rotate ~200 keys) to test per-key fairness and org aggregation. Running via k6 + our staging gateway. Example run command: ```k6 run --vus 100 --duration 1m scripts/rl_flood.js```

jonah: Also exercise routing policy: when primary pool hits capacity we should automatically fallback to lower-tier model variant AND emit header `X-Redwood-Fallback`. Capture that — fallback should not create a storm on Dedicated.

liam: Telemetry checklist: watch `rl.requests_total`, `rl.throttled`, `rl.requeued_to_fallback`, `rl.token_bucket_tokens` (per org tag), `gateway.upstream_503s`, and `gateway.429s`. I put a temporary read-only dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/rl-validate (token required).

sam: Quick q: for per-key tests, do we want to exercise shared org quotas too? We can spoof keys under the same org id; harness supports header override for `x-rw-org-id`.

maya: Yes — phase 3 will spoof ~50 keys under 3 orgs to validate per-org aggregation vs per-key caps. Keys will rotate every 10s to simulate client churn.

alex: Note: gateway currently returns 429 for quota exceed and 503 for backend resource exhaustion. API folks are debating switching to 429-only for consistency. For this run, capture both status codes and the `x-rw-rl-reason` header so we can feed the samples into the regression eval.

jonah: Also capture latency p50/p95/p99 and token burn rate per org. We'll compare to staging SLOs and look for tail regressions.

deploy-bot: Load test job scheduled: job-id=lt-20260318-01, scheduled_by=maya, scheduled_start_ts=1815003600, expected_duration=45m

liam: Heads-up — I'll enable detailed sampling on `rl.throttled` traces for 30m so we can see which keys are causing bursts. I'll tear it down after the test window.

maya: If anyone has other ongoing work in staging please pause or comment here. If we see production-proxied routing anomalies I'll abort immediately. ping @eng-sre.

sam: :eyes: I'll be watching logs and will escalate if we hit ticket noise. If needed I can flip the graceful-fallback off during the run.

alex: Putting the k6 script + key-rotation helper in the staging-runner repo: https://git.internal/staging-runner/lt-rl. Script includes a `--org-id` flag to batch requests under a single org.

jonah: After the run let's do a 30m sync to review dashboards, traces, and adjust RL params (burst size, fill rate, per-key windows). I want to see concrete numbers before we tweak defaults.

maya: Thanks — starting warmup now (gentle 10 RPS for 2m). Will post a short results snippet and any immediate red flags when warmup finishes.

sam: If we start seeing >5% retry loops in clients, I'll kill the run.

deploy-bot: job-started: job-id=lt-20260318-01, started_ts=1815003601

maya: Warmup done — no obvious 503 spikes, token burn looks normal. Kicking phase 1 in 2m. Will upload raw logs to the run artifact bucket when complete.

liam: Logged the trace sampling and dashboard alerts. If anyone needs temporary access to the dashboard ping me and I'll grant read-only.

alex: Small note for data collection: include `x-rw-key-id`, `x-rw-org-id`, `x-rw-rl-reason`, and response status in the metrics tagset so we can pivot quickly.

jonah: Good. Also capture gateway internal queue lengths — if those climb high we might need to reduce burst window or increase burst tokens.

maya: End-of-run plan: post a 2–3 line summary here + link to artifact + suggested parameter changes. Then we can schedule the follow-up sync.

sam: See you on the review. Good luck.
